story.summary: Create tests to use Home screen icons
story.description:
As an Organization user, I want to view and access only the eCore modules authorized for my organization, so that I can navigate to New Transaction, Workspace, and Preferences from the Dashboard main screen; access Home, New Transaction, Workspace, and Preferences from the top-right navigation menu; access Organization and Vault as sub-items under Preferences; and return to the Home page using Command Center.
The UI and supporting APIs must provide consistent module access and prevent unauthenticated or unauthorized access.

requirements.description: An Organization user sees and can access only the eCore modules that are authorized for their organization. Modules that are not authorized are not available to them.
requirements.originalText: As an Organization user, I want to view and access only the eCore modules authorized for my organization

requirements.description: From the Dashboard main screen, an Organization user can navigate to New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences.
requirements.originalText: so that I can navigate to New Transaction, Workspace, and Preferences from the Dashboard main screen

requirements.description: From the top-right navigation menu, an Organization user can access Home, New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences.
requirements.originalText: access Home, New Transaction, Workspace, and Preferences from the top-right navigation menu

requirements.description: Organization and Vault are reachable as sub-items under Preferences.
requirements.originalText: access Organization and Vault as sub-items under Preferences

requirements.description: An Organization user can return to the Home page using Command Center.
requirements.originalText: and return to the Home page using Command Center

requirements.description: The UI and the supporting APIs provide consistent module access, so that what a user may reach through the interface and what the same user may reach through the APIs agree with one another.
requirements.originalText: The UI and supporting APIs must provide consistent module access

requirements.description: The UI and the supporting APIs prevent unauthenticated access and prevent unauthorized access.
requirements.originalText: and prevent unauthenticated or unauthorized access

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each of the six named modules is present and can be opened by a signed-in Organization user.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Organization user is signed in to eCore
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user views the modules offered on the Home page and in the top-right navigation menu
acceptanceCriteria.then: each of Home, New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences, Organization and Vault is present and can be opened
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Covers the presence half of REQ-ETA-411-001 only, following the scope narrowing to the six named modules on 2026-09-05. The word 'only' in that requirement is an absence claim and is deliberately NOT covered here; it is carried by AC-ETA-411-002, which is blocked. Recording this criterion as satisfying REQ-ETA-411-001 in full would overstate coverage.

acceptanceCriteria.description: DEFERRED. No module outside the organization's authorized set is offered to the user.
acceptanceCriteria.given: DEFERRED - an organization whose authorized module set has been stated
acceptanceCriteria.when: DEFERRED - a user of that organization views the available modules
acceptanceCriteria.then: DEFERRED - no module outside that organization's authorized set is present or reachable
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Deferred by the scope narrowing recorded in AMB-ETA-411-002, not satisfied by it. This is the half of REQ-ETA-411-001 carrying the actual authorization claim: the account can reach nineteen navigable destinations while the ticket names six, and no organization-to-module mapping exists. It is kept in the artifact so that REQ-ETA-411-001 reports as partially covered rather than fully covered.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The Dashboard offers New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences, and each opens its module.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Organization user is signed in and is on the Home page
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user selects New Transaction, Workspace or Preferences from the Dashboard icons
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Directly stated by the story and corroborated by walked evidence in reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json, where the Dashboard icon container held exactly these three links and each was clicked through to its destination.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The top-right navigation menu offers Home, New Transaction and Workspace, and each opens its module.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Organization user is signed in
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the top-right navigation menu and selects Home, New Transaction or Workspace
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Covers only the three menu entries that observation confirms exist as navigable links. The story also lists Preferences as a menu entry; that part is split into AC-ETA-411-005 because the evidence contradicts it.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Preferences is offered in the navigation menu, with Organization and Vault grouped beneath it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Organization user is signed in
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the navigation menu
acceptanceCriteria.then: Preferences is offered, with Organization and Vault grouped beneath it
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Written as a presence check rather than a navigation check, per the resolution of AMB-ETA-411-007. The owner confirmed the menu displays Preferences among its entries, while the probe records no navigable link with that label, which is consistent with Preferences being a group heading over Organization and Vault. Asserting that Preferences opens a page of its own would go beyond both the ticket and the evidence; reaching Organization and Vault is covered by AC-ETA-411-006.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Organization and Vault are offered as sub-items under Preferences and each opens its page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Organization user is signed in
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user opens the top-right navigation menu and selects Organization or Vault under Preferences
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Stated by the story and corroborated by observation, which records both entries grouped beneath Preferences. Note for the planner: Organization resolves to the same destination as the Dashboard Preferences icon, so arrival must be asserted on page content rather than on destination alone.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Selecting Command Center from any of the six modules returns the user to the Home page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an Organization user is signed in and has navigated away from the Home page
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Home page is displayed again
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Stated by the story and corroborated by walked evidence, in which every navigation returned to the Home page. Note for the planner: the Command Center control carries no accessible name, so its locator will require a VALIDATED waiver under SEM-AUTOMATION-HYGIENE.

acceptanceCriteria.description: DEFERRED. The UI and the supporting APIs give consistent module access.
acceptanceCriteria.given: DEFERRED - a definition of consistent that can be observed
acceptanceCriteria.when: DEFERRED - the same user's module access is compared across the UI and the supporting APIs
acceptanceCriteria.then: DEFERRED - the stated consistency condition holds
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: Deferred by the owner on 2026-09-05 via AMB-ETA-411-005. REQ-ETA-411-006 is consequently recorded as UNCOVERED, not met. Even had it not been deferred it would be blocked twice: existing evidence suggests the six destinations are plain document requests rather than a distinct API layer, and anything discovered by observation is OBSERVED and may never judge an acceptance criterion.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An unauthenticated visitor requesting a module is shown an error message and remains on the sign-in page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a visitor who is not signed in, in a fresh browser session
acceptanceCriteria.when: the visitor requests a module directly
acceptanceCriteria.then: an error message is shown and the visitor remains on the sign-in page
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: The expected outcome was stated by the owner on 2026-09-05 and is recorded in AMB-ETA-411-004. This is the only negative path producible this release, since it needs neither an unauthorized module nor a second organization. Two assertions carry it: an error message is present, and the sign-in page is still the current page. The exact message text is captured as OBSERVED at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION and must be approved at Gate 2 before it is asserted, so that whatever the application happens to say today does not silently become the definition of correct.

acceptanceCriteria.description: DEFERRED AND UNPRODUCIBLE THIS RELEASE. An authenticated but unauthorized user is refused a module.
acceptanceCriteria.given: DEFERRED - a module this account is not authorized for
acceptanceCriteria.when: DEFERRED - the signed-in user requests that module
acceptanceCriteria.then: DEFERRED - the refusal is shown, identified by the approved message or element
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: A consequence of the scope narrowing in AMB-ETA-411-002 rather than a gap in the story. With scope limited to the six modules the account is authorized for, no unauthorized module remains to request, so this criterion cannot be produced at all this release regardless of the expected outcome being known. It is kept rather than dropped so that REQ-ETA-411-007 reports as partially covered.

ambiguities.question: LARGELY ANSWERED BY ACTION, PENDING ATTRIBUTION. This asked whether the rewritten description was a genuine reopening of ETA-411 or whether the scope belonged on a new child of ETA-164. On 2026-09-04 the story was moved from Closed to Open (statusCategory Done to To Do) and its ETA-164 parent link was removed, both verified by re-fetching and diffing the snapshot rather than taken on report. ETA-411 is therefore a genuine reopening and is now a standalone story, so the workflow id and the home-navigation capability partition are correctly attached. Residual: this resolution needs a named human recorded in resolvedBy, and the two Jira comments remain descriptions of this POC framework rather than of eCore, so their exclusion from the requirements still needs confirming.
ambiguities.impact: Scope and traceability. Now low: the reopening is confirmed by the tracker itself. Only the formal attribution and the comment-exclusion confirmation remain.
ambiguities.resolution: Confirmed by action in the tracker rather than by assertion: on 2026-09-04 ETA-411 was moved from Closed to Open and its ETA-164 parent link was removed, both verified by re-fetching and diffing the snapshot. ETA-411 is a genuine reopening and is now a standalone story, so the workflow id WF-ETA-411-R1.0 and the home-navigation capability partition are correctly attached. The two Jira comments remain excluded from the requirements because both describe the delivery of this POC framework rather than any eCore behaviour; that exclusion was put to the owner three times and not objected to.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)

ambiguities.question: ANSWERED AS A SCOPE NARROWING, PENDING ATTRIBUTION. This asked which organizations exist and which modules each may see. On 2026-09-05 the repository owner scoped it down: verify the six named modules only for now (Home, New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences, Organization, Vault), and do not attempt the organization-to-module mapping. This is a workable scope but it does not make REQ-ETA-411-001 fully testable, and the artifact must not pretend otherwise. The word 'only' in that requirement is an ABSENCE claim: the application exposes nineteen navigable destinations to the test account, and asserting that six of them are present and openable says nothing about whether the other thirteen should have been hidden. Residual: confirm that REQ-ETA-411-001 is to be recorded as PARTIALLY covered, with the absence half explicitly out of scope for this release rather than silently counted as covered.
ambiguities.impact: Presence and openability of the six modules is now testable. The authorization claim itself is not, and any coverage figure must show REQ-ETA-411-001 as partial. Reporting it as covered would be the exact failure this framework exists to prevent: a green result standing in for a check nobody ran.
ambiguities.resolution: Scope narrowed by the repository owner on 2026-09-05: verify only the six modules named in the ticket, and do not attempt an organization-to-module mapping this release. The consequence is recorded rather than hidden. REQ-ETA-411-001 is only PARTIALLY covered, because the word 'only' in it is an absence claim and the test account can reach nineteen navigable destinations while the ticket names six. AC-ETA-411-001 covers the presence half; AC-ETA-411-002 carries the absence half and is deferred, so it is never counted as covered.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)

ambiguities.question: ANSWERED AS A DISCOVERY INSTRUCTION, PENDING ATTRIBUTION AND A GATE 2 DECISION. On 2026-09-05 the repository owner defined the supporting APIs as whatever the application calls while navigating the six links. That is a legitimate way to find the surface, and it will be captured at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION. Two consequences must be stated plainly. First, existing evidence in reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json is that all six destinations are full document requests to .eo pages, so the capture may find no distinct API layer at all, in which case REQ-ETA-411-006 and REQ-ETA-411-007 have no API to test and should be deferred rather than faked. Second, anything captured this way is contractSource OBSERVED, which records what the application does, not what it should do; SEM-API-CONTRACT permits OBSERVED to seed a scenario into a state but never to judge an acceptance criterion. Residual: whether the captured contract is promoted to HUMAN_APPROVED at Gate 2, which is the only route by which it may be asserted against.
ambiguities.impact: Unblocks discovery, not assertion. Until a captured contract is approved at Gate 2, no API acceptance criterion for REQ-ETA-411-006 or REQ-ETA-411-007 can pass honestly, and the interface scenarios stay deferred.
ambiguities.resolution: Defined by the repository owner on 2026-09-05 as whatever the application calls while navigating to the six ticket links, to be captured at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION. Two limits travel with that definition. Anything captured is contractSource OBSERVED, which under SEM-API-CONTRACT may seed a scenario into a state but may never judge an acceptance criterion unless a human promotes it to HUMAN_APPROVED at Gate 2. And existing walk evidence indicates all six destinations are full document requests to .eo pages, so the capture may find no distinct API layer at all, in which case the API criteria are deferred rather than fabricated.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)

ambiguities.question: PARTIALLY ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER NEEDS A GATE 2 DECISION BEFORE IT CAN BE USED. On 2026-09-05 the repository owner stated that unauthorized access produces an error message on screen, and then directed that whatever text appears should be verified. Capturing the text is fine and will happen at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION. Asserting it is not automatically fine: taking the string the application currently emits and declaring it the expected outcome makes today's behaviour the definition of correct, so if that message is itself wrong, or later regresses to a different wrong message, the test would have to be edited to stay green and would never report a defect. The governed route is capture as OBSERVED, present the exact string in the Gate 2 review package, and only assert it once a human has approved that string, at which point it is HUMAN_APPROVED and authoritative. Residual: the unauthenticated case was still not answered separately, and the exact captured string needs Gate 2 approval.
ambiguities.impact: Only the unauthenticated path is reachable. With scope narrowed to the six modules the account is authorized for, no unauthorized module is available to navigate to, so the unauthorized half of REQ-ETA-411-007 cannot be produced at all this release and must be deferred rather than counted. The unauthenticated path can be produced today with a fresh browser context and is the one runnable negative scenario.
ambiguities.resolution: Answered by the repository owner on 2026-09-05. UNAUTHENTICATED: the visitor is shown an error message and remains on the sign-in page. Both halves are assertable, which is what makes this the one runnable negative scenario this release. Recorded caveat: the owner punctuated this answer with a question mark, so it is treated as their stated expectation and will be checked against observation at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION; if the application contradicts it, that is reported as a mismatch and never used to silently rewrite this expectation. UNAUTHORIZED: not producible this release, because scope was narrowed to the six modules the account is authorized for, leaving no unauthorized module to request; AC-ETA-411-010 is deferred. The exact refusal text is captured as OBSERVED and must be approved at Gate 2 before it is ever asserted, so that a wrong message today cannot become the definition of correct.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)

ambiguities.question: REQ-ETA-411-006 requires 'consistent module access' between the UI and the supporting APIs. What does consistent mean in a way that can be observed and asserted: identical module lists, identical allow and deny decisions for the same user, or something narrower?
ambiguities.impact: Without a definition this requirement cannot be turned into an acceptance criterion that can pass or fail honestly.
ambiguities.resolution: Deferred by the repository owner on 2026-09-05. A definition of consistent module access between the UI and the supporting APIs is not required this release. AC-ETA-411-008 is deferred with it, and REQ-ETA-411-006 is therefore recorded as UNCOVERED. Deferring the question is not the same as satisfying it, and no coverage figure may treat it as met.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)

ambiguities.question: ANSWERED IN PRINCIPLE, NOT YET IN DETAIL. On 2026-09-05 the repository owner replied that some of these names are exact and some are conceptual, which establishes that the story mixes literal UI labels with descriptive prose but does not yet say which is which. Observed evidence in reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json narrows it: 'Dashboard main screen' and 'the Home page' both resolve to https://qa1.eoriginal.org:8443/ssweb/setup/welcome.eo, and every walk returned to that same URL, so they appear to be one screen under two descriptions; 'Command Center' is a div with id bannerBackground and class clickable, carrying the command_center.png background image and no text, no aria-label, no title and no role, so it is a conceptual name for an unlabelled banner control rather than a literal label. Residual: confirm that reading, specifically that Dashboard main screen and Home page are the same screen and that Command Center means that banner.
ambiguities.impact: Determines how many destinations exist and how arrival is asserted. It also has a locator consequence: the banner has no accessible name, so it cannot be reached by getByRole and any locator for it will need a VALIDATED waiver under SEM-AUTOMATION-HYGIENE.
ambiguities.resolution: Answered by the repository owner on 2026-09-05: the page displayed after sign-in is the Command Center page, and it may equally be called the Home page or the Dashboard. Dashboard main screen, the Home page and Command Center therefore all denote one screen, which matches observation, where every walk returned to the same URL under the title eOriginal Command Center. The control that returns the user to it is the banner carrying the command_center background image, which has no text, aria-label, title or role, so any locator for it will require a VALIDATED waiver under SEM-AUTOMATION-HYGIENE.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)

ambiguities.question: The story and the application disagree, and the disagreement must be settled by a human rather than by whichever one an agent happens to trust. REQ-ETA-411-003 states that the top-right navigation menu offers Home, New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences. Observation in reports/validation/ETA-411-home-icons-probe.json records no navigable link labelled Preferences in that menu at all: the menu's named links are Home, New Transaction, Workspace, a block of analytics entries, then Organization and Vault, then Tutorials, Support, About and Logout. That is consistent with Preferences being a non-clickable group heading above Organization and Vault, which is also how REQ-ETA-411-004 describes it. Which is correct: is the story wrong that Preferences is selectable from the menu, or is the application missing an entry it should have? A further detail for whoever answers: the menu's Organization entry resolves to the same destination as the Dashboard Preferences icon.
ambiguities.impact: Splits REQ-ETA-411-003. AC-ETA-411-004 covers the three menu entries that observation confirms; AC-ETA-411-005 holds the Preferences entry and is blocked. If the story is right this is a product defect and no test should be written that passes today. If the application is right the story wording needs correcting.
ambiguities.resolution: Answered by the repository owner on 2026-09-05: the navigation menu does display Home, New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences and further entries, and only the items named in the ticket are to be verified. AC-ETA-411-005 is therefore written as a presence check on Preferences within the menu rather than a navigation check, because the probe records no navigable link with that label and the answer does not claim Preferences opens a page of its own; reaching Organization and Vault beneath it is already covered by AC-ETA-411-006. One discrepancy is recorded and is deliberately not settled by this answer: the ticket says top-right navigation menu while the owner described it as top left. The criterion follows the ticket wording, and menu position is a locator concern owned by the page object that does not change the behaviour being asserted.
ambiguities.resolvedBy: Anil.Maddhesia@wolterskluwer.com (repository owner; identity taken from the git commit author on this branch, answered in chat on 2026-09-05)
